done_when: forge fix start takes --slug to name the fix. forge fix amend <fix> --done "<text>" --because "<why>" replaces the fix's Done-when, keeps the old text and the reason in the fix's record, and the next review judges the new text.

findings.body: When a fix already has a pull request, this changes the recorded Done-when and the next review prompt, but the pull request still displays the old text. `src/forge/close.py:281` writes the original `Done when:` line, while `src/forge/close.py:291-296` updates only the marked review block on later closes. A reviewer reading the pull request therefore sees a requirement the fix no longer has. Refresh that line when publishing the amended review.
findings.title: Update an existing pull request’s Done-when after amendment

findings.body: `close._worktree` also resolves task worktrees (`src/forge/close.py:158-166`), so `forge fix amend SHOP/T1 ...` succeeds and writes a Done-when into a task record. The next task review instead takes its criteria from the story document (`src/forge/review.py:205-222`), making the command’s success message false for that item. Check that the resolved state is a fix before changing it.
findings.title: Reject non-fix items in fix amend

why: A fix's name comes from its why-text and is often long and cut mid-word, and a fix's Done-when can't be changed when part of the fix moves elsewhere, so reviews keep flagging the original text
